rule: S_N must not contain null values.
rationale: S_N is the primary join key linking to other tables; null values would break joins.

rule: All S_N values must be unique.
rationale: S_N is a one‑to‑one join key; uniqueness guarantees a reliable link to Acc_Info_dirty.

rule: Account_No must be a four‑digit numeric string.
rationale: The column is intended to be a string identifier of exactly four characters; all observed values follow this pattern.

rule: ID_No should follow the dominant pattern: a leading letter, seven digits, and a trailing letter (e.g., S1234567D).
rationale: 93 % of records match this pattern; deviations should be clarified with the data owner.

rule: Race must be one of the canonical categories: Chinese, Malay, Indian.
rationale: Observed values are variations of these three races; standardising case and limiting to these values removes noise.

rule: Gender must be either 'Male' or 'Female'.
rationale: All records represent binary gender; case variations are normalised to title case.

rule: Age must be between 0 and 120 inclusive.
rationale: A realistic human age range; the observed minimum is -5 (invalid) and maximum 66, so a domain constraint is appropriate.

rule: Flag records where Age cannot be parsed as a numeric value.
rationale: One record contains the literal string 'Twenty-five', which is not parseable as a number.

rule: Flag ages that are less than 13, which are unlikely for a consumer‑service account.
rationale: Two records have ages 4 and -5; business logic suggests a minimum service age of 13.

rule: Email must match the simple email pattern: local-part@domain.
rationale: Four records are malformed (missing '@' or containing spaces); a lightweight regex catches these cases without over‑restricting.

rule: Contact_No must not be null.
rationale: 2 out of 30 records are missing a phone number; contact information is required for downstream communications.

rule: Contact_No must follow a Singapore phone format: '+65 12345678', '65 12345678' or an 8‑digit local number.
rationale: Observed patterns include international (+65), local with prefix (65) and plain 8‑digit numbers; all should be convertible to the international format.

rule: Country must be one of the observed Singapore representations.
rationale: All records refer to Singapore but use eight different textual variants; enumerating the observed set captures current data while highlighting the need for canonicalisation.

rule: Flag names that are not in title case (e.g., all‑upper or all‑lower).
rationale: The dataset contains mixed casing; business rules require title‑case for consistency.

check_params.logic: any(not w.istitle() for w in str(row['Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','s/o','d/o'))

rule: Gender must be consistent with name particles: 'Bin' or 's/o' imply Male; 'Binte' or 'd/o' imply Female.
rationale: Cultural naming conventions encode gender; mismatches indicate data entry errors.

check_params.logic: ((bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])\ bin\ (?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower())) or str(row['Name']).lower().endswith(' bin') or bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])\ s/o\ (?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower()))) and str(row['Gender']).lower() != 'male') or ((bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])\ binte\ (?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower())) or bool(re.search(r'(?<![a-z0-9])\ d/o\ (?![a-z0-9])', str(str(row['Name'])).lower()))) and str(row['Gender']).lower() != 'female')

rule: Postal_Code must be a numeric string of length 4 to 6.
rationale: Postal codes are stored as integers but should be treated as strings; lengths observed between 4‑6 digits.

rule: Postal_Code must be a 6-digit code
rationale: Singapore postal codes are uniformly six digits; shorter codes indicate data quality issues.

rule: Every S_N in Cust_Bio_dirty must exist in Acc_Info_dirty.S_N.
rationale: S_N is a one‑to‑one join key; referential integrity ensures records can be linked across tables.

rule: JoinDate must not be later than LastLogin.
rationale: A customer cannot log in before their account is created; ordering validates temporal consistency.

rationale: Column is 93.3% distinct with duplicate value(s) [1001, 1010] observed; treated as a candidate identifier — duplicates flagged for review.
